stories.headline: Caleb Wilson and a new regime: The summer that changed the Chicago Bulls
stories.summary: It has been an offseason of change in Chicago. Now, No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson and a new Bulls front office have turned the tide for a franchise lost in the middle.
stories.body:
IT'S AUG. 22 and Chicago Bulls fans pack the area surrounding the United Center. The team is hosting its annual two-day fan festival, Bulls fest, and fans are lining up for the chance to meet the 20-year-old who has not only provided a new, unfamiliar hope around the franchise this summer but someone to pull the franchise out of a decade of irrelevance. This is Caleb Wilson's introduction to Chicago.

The lines for his meet-and-greet wrap around the atrium. The next event of the fest is a slam dunk contest in the parking lot, where Wilson is one of the judges. But first, he screams and sticks his tongue out for a hype video in front of a crowd of fans standing in front of the Michael Jordan statue.

The image -- a juxtaposition from where the franchise once was and where it now plans to go -- is impossible to ignore.

The anticipation has been growing for months, ever since the Bulls selected the North Carolina star No. 4 overall during the NBA draft in June.

The Bulls hope Wilson is the new face of the franchise, a much-needed refresh for a team that has missed the playoffs in eight of the past nine seasons.

The hype began to boil after Wilson's electric showing during his first in-game action at the Las Vegas summer league. Wilson finished his first professional game with 35 points, the second-highest total for a rookie debut in summer league history, and knocked down seven 3-pointers in the process.

In his second game, Wilson soared over 6-foot-11 Jazz center Jonas Aidoo to throw down an emphatic dunk in one of the top highlight-reel plays of the summer.

By his fourth and final game, Hall of Fame forward Kevin Garnett sat courtside to get a glimpse of the rookie to whom he started to draw comparisons. Both are 6-foot-10, wiry 215-pound players buoyed by elite athleticism. "I actually think his floor is Kevin Garnett," Warriors forward Draymond Green said on his podcast this summer.

"And man, if that's your floor, oh my god. Do you know how great KG was? I actually think with Caleb Wilson, Kevin Garnett could be his floor. That's how special I think Caleb Wilson is."

Teams are normally hesitant to make grand proclamations from summer league, but Wilson's performance stood out.

"He looks," one team source told ESPN, "like we got a dude."

The Bulls believe Wilson is yet another new pillar of an almost entirely new leadership structure. They hired a new head of basketball operations, Bryson Graham, who had a reputation for building through the draft and finding young talent.

Graham then selected a new head coach, Tiago Splitter, who has a background of player development success stories. They selected Wilson and then rounded out the roster with veterans such as Norman Powell and Nic Claxton, but Wilson's development will be the franchise's top priority in the 2026-27 season.

"We just want to see internal growth from our young guys and even from our veteran players," Graham told ESPN. "We just want to see a team that's going to go out there, represent this city well, play hard and obviously continue to grow and continue to develop."

Though expectations are high for Wilson across the league, team sources said there is no pressure for the Bulls to compete for a play-in or playoff spot in a loaded Eastern Conference. After years of the Bulls trying to jump-start themselves back into relevance, the decision-makers in Chicago are preaching patience before a resurrection.

For his part, though, Wilson has made his goals for his rookie season clear.

"I expect to have Rookie of the Year, honestly," Wilson said. "I'm going to work hard. I'm going to do what it takes. I feel like the team is really good for me and how I envision to play."

THE SUMMER LEAGUE debut was eye-popping in a smaller, but even more tantalizing, way.

Wilson's seven made 3s were more than he made during his entire freshman season at North Carolina.

Concerns about his shooting ability -- along with an injury that shortened his college season and kept him out of the NCAA tournament -- were the biggest knocks against him entering the draft and why he was ultimately selected behind AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer in the 2026 draft class.

To explain and perhaps ease those concerns, Wilson pointed to the system at North Carolina, one that did not ask him to take 3-pointers (he averaged 1.1 attempts per game), but he also noted how he began working to improve his shot once the college season ended.

"I'm glad I didn't shoot 3s in college," Wilson said after a practice this summer. "Because if I did, I wouldn't be here. I don't know where I'd be. I don't think I'd be a Bull."

A broken thumb and left wrist fracture ended Wilson's college season in February, and he couldn't move his thumb while wearing a cast that kept the digit straight. But he could still hold a ball to practice his form, and he did so -- over and over, all summer.

Wilson estimates he has been shooting between 2,000 and 2,500 3-pointers per day.

For as much as Wilson's performance on the court generated buzz throughout the league, his work ethic has only heightened the excitement inside the organization.

He cried before his professional debut, five months to the day since the end of his college season, because he said he had been waiting for that moment for so long. The other top picks in his class were shut down from action after two or three summer league games, but Wilson pushed to keep playing, texting Graham to ask to play on the second night of a back-to-back in Chicago's third game of the summer.

Wilson averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 2.5 blocks in four summer league games at and was named to the all-summer league first team. When informed that his 35-point debut was one of the highest-scoring debut performances in the history of the event, Wilson shrugged it off because his team lost.

Outside of his time in Las Vegas, Wilson has been a mainstay in Chicago since the draft. He works out at the team's practice facility in the morning and then returns around 8 or 9 p.m., along with fellow first-round pick Dailyn Swain, who was selected No. 15 by Chicago in June, for workouts that routinely approach midnight.

"Everybody highlights his athleticism, which is generational," Swain said. "But he can do a lot of things. He's really good facing up at the elbow, jab. He has a really good midrange shot. He's been knocking down 3s, so he's widening his arsenal."

GRAHAM'S FIRST MAJOR hire as the team's head of basketball operations was to bring in Splitter, a coach whose vision Graham touted as close to his own.

As an interim coach last season, Splitter led the Portland Trail Blazers to a surprise playoff appearance as the No. 7 seed in the Western Conference, but during his introductory news conference in Chicago, neither Splitter nor Graham focused on repeating such an unlikely jump.

Graham touted Splitter's player development credentials, from helping Deni Avdija become an All-Star in Portland to his days as an assistant coach, guiding Jarrett Allen as a member of the Brooklyn Nets' player development staff in 2019 or a young Alperen Sengun as an assistant with the Houston Rockets in 2023.

"The first thing you do is connect," Splitter said. "That's the foundation of everything you do, especially at this level. If you don't have that, it's really hard to demand and make them respect you. The foundation is [to] connect with the players in different ways."

Splitter started his bond with Wilson early this summer. It began with a shared interest in music and with Splitter being surprised at Wilson's range in music tastes. The 19-year-old began learning the guitar in his spare time this summer and has played everything from hip-hop to classical to country.

"Very interesting young guy," Splitter said. "You see how his brain functions and the variety of things he can have a conversation about."

Splitter also stepped in to coach the Bulls at summer league for the team's first two games in Las Vegas. He said he wanted the opportunity to establish a culture with his young players. For a young coach still finding his identity, it was good practice for the challenge of taking over a franchise starved for a winner with newfound expectations of the future.

"He's really detailed," Wilson said. "He knows what he wants you to do and he's pretty serious. Most coaches, you have coaches that are joking around and stuff like that. Tiago's pretty serious and he knows what he wants.

"I'd rather have someone who's serious and straightforward with me, so I know what I can do better."

Wilson functioned as the team's point guard and primary ball handler for most of the summer -- something that wasn't featured in Garnett's Hall of Fame career -- but those duties will lessen by the start of the season when he's surrounded by Josh Giddey, Powell and third-year forward Matas Buzelis, who will help run the offense after starting 77 games last season.

"It builds a healthy environment," Graham said. "It gives the younger guys confidence, too, because they know that, when it is going bad, they have some guys that have done it, some guys that have won and had success and they can learn. It's just really important for the overall development of our younger players and the health of our team."

In his previous experiences as a head coach, Splitter has been malleable in his style of play.

He coached in France and led Paris Basketball, a club in the first division of French basketball, to the EuroLeague playoffs with a fast-paced offense.

With the Blazers a season ago, defense became the calling card. Chicago represents his first chance to shape a young roster in his own image.

"You have to adapt your system to the players you have," Splitter said.

"Yes, I have a vision. I have a certain way I want to play, but you also have to explore what they do best. That's what we're going to do here."

It's what Splitter was hired to accomplish -- to help nurture and guide Chicago's roster while its young players develop.

In what has become an annual tradition, Bulls players convened in Miami last week for a player-run minicamp a few weeks before training camp.

And as the hype for Wilson continues to rise, the Bulls rookie remains focused on his ultimate goal.

"I do expect to win," he said. "Whatever it takes to win is what I'm going to do."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Spurs to make late move for Pulisic?
stories.summary: The deadline for the summer window in Europe closes tomorrow, and Tottenham Hotspur are interested in AC Milan winger Christian Pulisic. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
USMNT and AC Milan winger Christian Pulisic is of interest to Tottenham Hotspur, while AC Milan have Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Barcelona left back Alejandro Balde. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Tottenham Hotspur are interested in AC Milan winger Christian Pulisic, according to TEAMtalk. It is reported that the Premier League side have made an inquiry for the 27-year-old, having identified him as a potential alternative signing to Liverpool winger and Manchester City-linked Cody Gakpo. Spurs are among multiple teams to have checked on the situation of USMNT star Pulisic, who played no part in the 2-0 Serie A win over Venezia on Friday as he continues his return from injury.

- Chelsea have made AS Roma midfielder Manu Koné their priority target to replace Enzo Fernández, says Footmercato. Koné, 25, has been linked with a €40 million exit all summer, but Argentina international Fernández completes a £120 million move to Manchester City before the window shuts, then

- AC Milan have Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Barcelona left back Alejandro Balde on their shortlist, Tuttosport reports. Yoro, 20 is reportedly among several players being considered by the Rossoneri, who are exploring the market for defenders, with plans to offload Fikayo Tomori and find a long term option at full back. It is reported that a move for 22-year-old Balde would require an offer worth around €50 million.

- Barcelona are monitoring the situation of Internazionale wing back Federico Dimarco, Gazzetta dello Sport reports. The Blaugrana see the 28-year-old as a key starter due to his ability in the attacking third, but aware of growing interest from the LaLiga club, the Nerazzurri are now considering talks to sign him to a new contract extension. Dimarco made 46 appearances across all competitions for Inter last season.

- Chelsea, Aston Villa, and Newcastle are looking at Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane, Football Insider reports. All three sides are reportedly exploring a swoop to sign the 20-year-old before the transfer window closes on Tuesday, with the Blues viewing him as a high-potential prospect for the future. Kofane began the new Bundesliga campaign with a goal when coming on as a substitute to score in the 3-2 defeat against SV Elversberg on Saturday.

- Liverpool are lining up a €35 million approach for Genk goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans, according to the Liverpool Echo. The Reds have identified the 18-year-old as a potential replacement for Giorgi Mamardashvili, who is attracting interest from Nottingham Forest. A move for Brughmans is expected to be difficult, with Real Madrid among multiple clubs in Europe keeping tabs on his situation. The 6-foot-6 stopper has been capped twice by Belgium as a youth international at U19 level. Liverpool have also agreed a deal to sign 18-year-old striker Djylian N'Guessan from Saint Etienne next summer, according to Fabrizio Romano.

ESPN sources
- Fiorentina are set to sign striker Beto from Everton for a fee in the region of £15 million. Beto, 28, is set to have his medical in Florence on Monday and his departure could prompt Everton to move for United States forward Folarin Balogun. Read

- Barcelona are in "very advanced" negotiations with Arsenal over a deal to sign Brazilian striker Gabriel Jesus. Jesus, 29, has just one year to run on his contract with the English champions and has emerged as an option for Barça following their failure to land Julián Álvarez. Read

- Women's Super League (WSL) side Manchester United are finalizing a deal to sign Mexico international Rebeca Bernal from the NWSL's Washington Spirit. According to the source, an announcement is expected at some point ahead of Manchester United's season-opener on Sept. 4. Read

Done deals
- Manchester City have signed Germany international right back Carlotta Wamser from Bayer Leverkusen. Read

- England international striker Ollie Watkins has joined Al Hilal from Aston Villa for around £51 million, the Saudi Pro League club announced. Read

Other rumors
- Manchester United striker Marcus Rashford wants to stay put despite interest from Chelsea, Newcastle and Aston Villa. (Football Insider)

- VfB Stuttgart winger Jamie Leweling, 25, is on the radar of Liverpool, Everton, and Roma over a loan which includes an obligation to be made permanent for €40 million (Patrick Berger)

- Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have shown interest in Al Hilal striker Karim Benzema. (Diario AS)

- Atletico Madrid have made a new approach for Juventus and Canada international striker Jonathan David. The Serie A club see Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee as his potential successor. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Valencia are optimistic of securing a deal to sign Liverpool attacking midfielder Harvey Elliott. (Matteo Moretto)

- Juventus are keen to keep hold of midfielder Nico Gonzalez amid interest from Atletico Madrid. (Marca)

- Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to loan defender Honest Ahanor, who is set to complete a €40 million switch from Atalanta to Chelsea. (Di Marzio)

- Newcastle and Sunderland could battle for the signature of Roma winger Matias Soule. (TEAMtalk)

- Aston Villa have been informed that a £25 million offer would be required to land Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. (Football Insider)

- Sunderland are discussing a loan move for Tottenham Hotspur defender Kevin Danso. (Telegraph)

- Everton striker Beto is set to complete a €17 million switch to Fiorentina. (Fabrizio Romano)

Aug. 31: Monday's news to know
By Todd Zola

A dozen evening affairs comprise a relatively busy Monday docket, beginning at 6:05 p.m. ET with the San Francisco Giants visiting the Atlanta Braves. Overall this month, scoring has been trending down. However, early weather forecasts portend a high-scoring slate to close out play for August. Rain may be an issue, however, when the Colorado Rockies host the Baltimore Orioles at 8:40 p.m. ET.

Elly De La Cruz left yesterday's contest in the seventh inning with a tight left quad. After the game, Cincinnati Reds manager Terry Francona indicated the team didn't believe the injury was serious, suggesting the star shortstop could return to the lineup tonight for the opener of a home series with the San Diego Padres.
The Seattle Mariners are set to call up Lazaro Montes, the club's No. 4 prospect on Kiley McDaniel's updated 2026 top 10 prospect rankings for all 30 MLB teams. The 21-year-old outfielder began the season with Double-A Arkansas, posting a .234/.369/.550 line over 79 games. He has spent the last 43 games with Triple-A Tacoma, batting .267/.359/.564. Power is Montes' forte, but he must cut down on the over 30% strikeout rate he recorded at both minor league levels. He'll likely play right field, shifting Dominic Canzone to DH.
The Minnesota Twins finally placed Byron Buxton on the 10-day IL for his lingering hip issue. He missed four consecutive games prior to the move. Walker Jenkins has been handling center field and should play regularly while Buxton is out, which could be the rest of the season. Earlier in the year, it was reported that Buxton needs surgery on his hip. Instead of waiting for the offseason, he could be shut down soon and then go under the knife.
The St. Louis Cardinals will be without NL Rookie of the Year candidate JJ Wetherholt for at least 10-days after placing him on the IL due to right wrist tendinitis. Struggles over the past month have dropped him behind Sal Stewart in the race for freshman honors. Missing time may make it hard for him to make up ground with voters.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Monday.

Aug. 30: Sunday morning's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's schedule gets an early 12:15 p.m. ET start with the Washington Nationals entertaining the Miami Marlins. Thirteen matinees follow, with the fantasy period ending with the Cincinnati Reds visiting the Chicago Cubs at 7:20 p.m. ET. Due to a scheduling quirk, the Arizona Diamondbacks and San Francisco Giants have a rare Sunday off.

After several false alarms, Boston Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy indicated that Roman Anthony and Trevor Story are expected to be activated from the IL and join the club for the finale of a four-game series in the Bronx against the New York Yankees. Anthony's pathway to playing time is clearer, as he'll take over primary DH duties. Story will need to vie for action with Andruw Monasterio, Nick Sogard and Anthony Seigler.
The Yankees reported that the initial diagnosis of George Lombard Jr.'s knee injury is encouraging. The rookie shortstop hurt his knee on a swing during the second game of yesterday's doubleheader. Lombard's status will be updated after they finish evaluating his imaging. If Lombard is forced to miss action, Jose Caballero is the likely replacement.
The New York Mets reinstated Juan Soto from the 10-day IL prior to yesterday's game with the Houston Astros. He was sidelined for almost a month with a Grade 2 calf strain. Soto opted to skip a rehab assignment, but he still went 1-for-4 with a run and RBI in his return. The club cleared a roster spot by placing Luis Roberts on waivers. The veteran outfielder has been productive in August, but he's likely to clear waivers and potentially return to the Mets' active roster.
The Los Angeles Dodgers were hopeful that Shohei Ohtani would start today's road tilt with the Detroit Tigers. They expected only an inning or two, but after the two-way phenom cut short Friday's bullpen session, his return to the hill was delayed indefinitely. Tyler Glasnow is moving up a day to face the Tigers.

stories.headline: What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is facing 100 drivers in a unique event called Max vs. 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 challengers, starting from the back of the grid.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is taking part in a unique event called Max vs 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 drivers, starting from the back of the grid.

The 28-year-old currently races in F1, the highest tier in motorsport. He is one of the fiercest competitors out there and is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking.

But if you have never heard of him, or want to learn more, here is everything you need to know.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

Who is Max Verstappen?
Verstappen was born in Belgium to his Dutch father Jos and his Belgian mother Sophie. His father raced in F1 between 1994-2003 and had two podium finishes, while his mother competed in karts. He currently resides in Monaco.

Who does he race for?
Verstappen started racing go-karts when he was just four years old and started to compete in championships at seven.

He then made his way through the ranks winning several world and European titles in 2013. He raced just one season in Formula 3 before skipping Formula 2 and heading straight to Formula 1.

In 2015, he signed for Red Bull junior team Toro Rosso at the age of 17 before he was promoted to Red Bull a year later.

He then went on to become the youngest ever grand prix winner after taking victory at the Spanish Grand Prix and has been at Red Bull ever since, becoming the most successful driver at the team.

He signed a long-term contract back in March 2022 to stay at the Milton Keynes-based team until the end of 2028, and before the Dutch Grand Prix this year he penned a new deal keeping him at the team until 2030.

What has he achieved?
It was clear from the early days that Verstappen was going to be an exceptional racing driver and he's become a phenomenon since with a killer instinct.

He's had 244 race starts in F1 and has been on the top step of the podium 71 times. He's been on the podium 131 times and is just two pole positions away from reaching 50 career poles.

The Dutchman has four world championships which he won back-to-back in a dominant Red Bull era between 2021-2024.

He also has an impressive list of achievements to his name, one being in 2023 where he recorded the most wins [19] and the most podium finishes [21] in a single season. He also recorded 10 consecutive race victories.

When is Max vs 100?
The event is taking place on Sept. 16 and will be streamed live on Disney+.

Why is he racing in Max vs 100?

Verstappen has never been shy of getting his teeth stuck into other forms of motorsport away from Formula 1. He most recently made his debut at the iconic Nürburgring 24 Hours in May, driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3.

This will be a slightly different challenge for the Dutchman, but no doubt one he will enjoy with his competitive nature.

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," Verstappen said. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return."

The event is taking place at Silverstone in the U.K. and a circuit has been purpose-built for the occasion. It's set to be the biggest go-kart event in the world.

- Max Verstappen deal: Good news for Red Bull and F1, bad news for the driver market

- Max Verstappen ends F1 speculation by signing new Red Bull contract to 2030

How is his 2026 F1 season going?
The 2026 season is one with big regulation and rules changes and Red Bull are currently at the back of the front running teams, but are ahead of the midfield pack.

Verstappen is still searching for his first race win of the season, but has been on the podium four times.

He's currently sixth in the title championship and is 130 points adrift from title leader Kimi Antonelli.

stories.headline: Shepard has 22nd double-double this season, Wings beat Sun 97-71
stories.summary: — Arike Ogunbowale scored 18 points, Jessica Shepard had 17 points and 10 rebounds, and the Dallas Wings beat the Connecticut Sun 97-71 on Sunday night in the final game before the FIBA World Cup break.
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Arike Ogunbowale scored 18 points, Jessica Shepard had 17 points and 10 rebounds, and the Dallas Wings beat the Connecticut Sun 97-71 on Sunday night in the final game before the FIBA World Cup break.


The Wings (24-16) have won four in a row and have their most wins in a season since 2007, when the franchise also won 24 games as the Detroit Shock. The Shock won a franchise-record 25 games in 2003 on their way to the first of three WNBA championships.


Dallas moved into a three-way tie with New York and Washington for sixth in the WNBA standings, two games back of Indiana and Atlanta.


Shepard had her 22nd double-double this season, second most in the WNBA — after Angel Reese with 29 — to extend the franchise record. Paige Bueckers added 15 points and six assists and Maddy Siegrist scored 11 for Dallas.


Aaliyah Edwards scored 21 of her career-best tying 26 points in the first half for the Sun (10-30). Charlisse Leger-Walker hit five 3-pointers and finished with 17 points.


Saniya Rivers made a driving layup that gave the Sun their first lead about 4 1/2 minutes into the game at 11-10, but Bueckers scored inside 11 seconds later to put Dallas back in front for good.


Connecticut, which trailed by 13 at halftime, made 4 of 17 (23.5%) from the field, 1 of 6 from behind the arc, and hit 3 of 6 from the free-throw line as it was outscored 23-12 in the third quarter.


Up next
Sun: Plays Sept. 17 at Atlanta.


Wings: Host Los Angeles on Sept. 17.


----


This story has been updated to correct that the Shock won 24 games in 2007, not 24 straight.

In two early starts on the opening day, Club Brugge will host Aston Villa and AEK Athens will welcome LASK, the newcomers from Austria. Both games will kick off at 6:45 p.m.

One day later, defending champions Paris Saint-Germain will host Slovan Bratislava -- coached by Yaya Touré, the first African leading a team at the league phase -- and Liverpool will host Atlético Madrid, a repeat of their opening game last season. That was a 3-2 win for Liverpool at Anfield.

Debut-making Sabah of Azerbaijan will start at Manchester United on Sept. 10, the same day Como host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich welcome Bodo/Glimt.

Tough October for PSG
Manchester City hosting PSG on Oct. 14 is a highlight of the second round of games played more than one month later, after the new and extended four-game slate for national teams.

PSG will then face Barcelona at Parc des Princes on Oct. 20, one day before Bayern Munich host Arsenal.

Barcelona's next trip will then be a long way east to play Sabah in Baku on Nov. 25, before the Spanish champions hosts Man City on Dec. 8.

Arsenal will host Real Madrid on Dec. 9 for the first of coach Mourinho's scheduled two visits to London.

Madrid will return on the final match day, Jan. 27, to face Shakhtar Donetsk at Chelsea, where Mourinho won three Premier League titles for the club's Russian then-owner Roman Abramovich. Stamford Bridge is the Ukrainian champions' choice of neutral venue for its four home games.

Welcome to Norway
The two Norwegian teams each must have a home game in January, during their domestic offseason when the weather should be most severe, and both will be in the seventh round.

Bodo/Glimt will welcome Atlético Madrid to the Arctic Circle at their tiny stadium on Jan. 19 and Viking will host PSV Eindhoven in Stavanger one day later.

Final round
The final round on Jan. 27 sees all 18 games start at the same time, when it's 9 p.m. in central Europe, and Barcelona will host newcomers Como coached by their former star Cesc Fàbregas.

Como get the toughest January run-in after hosting PSG one week earlier.

PSG will finish by hosting Galatasaray, Arsenal will host Sabah and Bayern will host Real Betis.

The top eight teams in the final standings go directly to the round of 16 in March. Teams placed ninth to 24th enter the knockout playoffs in February to decide the other eight teams in the round of 16. Teams placed 25th to 36th are eliminated.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Song Yadong KO's Umar Nurmagomedov in massive UFC upset
stories.summary: Song Yadong pulled off a massive upset by knocking out heavily favored Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Shanghai.
stories.body:
Song Yadong saved the greatest performance of his career for his home country, knocking out former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Shanghai.

Song (24-9-1, 1 NC), a nearly 5-1 underdog at DraftKings Sportsbook, dropped Nurmagomedov with a short right hand, drawing a roar from the crowd when the fight was waved off at 1 minute, 48 seconds of Round 2.

"I believe in myself, and my team believed that I would win this fight," Song said through an interpreter. "They told me I would knock this guy out, and I did it."

It was the second straight fight in China for Song and his second straight win by finish. His most recent knockout win had been in 2023.

Song, making his first appearance in Shanghai since his UFC debut at age 19 in 2017, walked out to a hero's welcome.

"Nine years ago, I wanted to show I could walk in this Octagon," he said. "Nine years later, I want to prove I am the best in the world. I am the best Chinese fighter in the world."

The knockout came after Nurmagomedov (20-2) ducked out of the way of a left hand and right into the path of a short right hand, which connected near his right ear and sent him limply to the canvas. Song delivered three finishing shots on the mat before the referee jumped in.

That sent Song running around inside the cage in celebration, where he nearly ran into Nurmagomedov's younger brother and cornerman, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, who had rushed in to check on his fallen brother. Usman Nurmagomedov appeared to throw an elbow in Song's direction as the elated winner was running past.

Song climbed atop the cage to soak in the fans' cheers before jumping down outside the cage and running into the crowd to get hugs and high-fives from fans.

"Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not next month, but I will be the first male Chinese UFC champion," Song said through the interpreter, with the "male" designation a nod to countrywoman Zhang Weili, a two-time women's champion at strawweight.

Song, who trains in Sacramento, California, switched to English and yelled, "Give me the title shot!"

stories.headline: Avalanche's Makar agrees to record deal worth $20.4M annually
stories.summary: Cale Makar has agreed to an eight-year extension with the Avalanche that will make him the highest-paid player in NHL history with a $20.4 million average annual value.
stories.body:
Cale Makar has agreed to an eight-year extension with the Colorado Avalanche that will make him the highest-paid player in NHL history.

The deal carries a $20.4 million average annual value. Makar is the first player in league history to make at least $20 million per season. The max a player could make, per percentage of the salary cap, is $20.8 million.

Makar, 27, has been a finalist for the Norris Trophy as the league's top defenseman for six consecutive seasons. He is one of only 14 players to win multiple Norris Trophies, winning the award twice -- most recently in 2025.

Makar was entering the final year of his contract, which carried a $9 million average annual value.

The deal carries a full no-movement clause, according to sources. The eight-year term carries significance because when the new collective bargaining rules kick in Sept. 15, players will be able to sign for a maximum of only seven years.

This summer has seen record-breaking contracts in the NHL thanks to a rising salary cap, including massive deals for young centers Macklin Celebrini and Leo Carlsson.

Makar is a centerpiece for the Avalanche, perennial Stanley Cup contenders who won the Presidents' Trophy last season.

stories.headline: Knights prop ruled out of NRL finals with mammoth ban
stories.summary: Jacob Saifiti's NRL season is all but over after the Newcastle prop was handed a four-game suspension for a high tackle on Warriors winger Luke Laulilii.
stories.body:
Jacob Saifiti's NRL season is all but over after the Newcastle prop was handed a four-game suspension for a high tackle on Warriors winger Luke Laulilii.

Saifiti was sent off in the first half of Sunday's 46-32 defeat in Auckland and was handed a grade two reckless high tackle charge by the NRL's match review committee on Monday morning.

The Knights are on the bye for the final round of the regular season, meaning Saifiti's ban will only kick in for their first finals game.

Newcastle - currently sitting seventh - will play an elimination final in week one but even if they were to upset the odds and qualify for the grand final, the Fijian prop would still be on the sidelines with suspension.

Saifiti's only hope of playing in the NRL again this season hinge on the prop contesting the charge at the judiciary on Tuesday in a bid to reduce his punishment.

Should the front-rower fight the suspension and lose his appeal, he will have another week added to his four-game ban.

Elsewhere, Cronulla prop Tom Hazelton is set to miss Cronulla's final regular season game against Melbourne after being cited for a hip-drop tackle on Ronald Volkman.

Hazelton was sin-binned by referee Ashley Klein late in Sunday's loss to Parramatta but will serve a one-game ban with an early guilty plea and be free to return for week one of the final series.

stories.headline: Miami Heat offseason recap, early 2026-27 season preview
stories.summary: Miami landed Giannis to create one of the league's most dangerous frontcourts. What's next? We're recapping the offseason and taking an early look at 2026-27.
stories.body:
The Miami Heat have never shied away from chasing -- and landing -- superstars. Shaquille O'Neal in 2004. LeBron James and Chris Bosh in 2010. Jimmy Butler III in 2019. And this offseason, two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo, acquired via trade with the Milwaukee Bucks.

Those previous blockbuster summers produced NBA Finals appearances within two seasons. Can Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo, coach Erik Spoelstra and Miami follow suit? While the Heat continue to bolster the supporting cast, their roster might not yet be equipped to transform from a play-in team to a title threat.

So what will 2026-27 bring for one of the Eastern Conference's most intriguing franchises?

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for all 30 teams.

Quick links:

Roster | Depth chart | Transactions

More Heat coverage | More NBA

Offseason at a glance
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Zach Kram grades the Klay signing: B-

Thompson's on-court value no longer matches his name value, as a future Hall of Famer who was a centerpiece of the NBA's last great dynasty.

There's a reason, after all, that the Mavericks were amenable to buying Thompson out of the last year of his contract to pave his path to Miami. He is now 36 years old and nowhere near the sort of two-way star he was at his peak. Instead, the five-time All-Star is now a well below-average player.

But Thompson will bring one important skill to Miami that the Heat are currently lacking: Even as he has declined, he has remained an elite shooter. Thompson has made at least 38% of his 3-pointers on high volume in every season of his career, and even coming off the bench last season, he ranked among the top 20 players in made 3s per game.

Incidentally, Thompson ranked second in total 3s from a reserve last season -- one spot behind Hardaway, his new teammate on Miami's perimeter. -- Kram

What we learned over the past few months
From Ben Golliver's offseason lessons piece: Riley's still got it.

Landing Antetokounmpo meant taking on his injury risks and parting with four players and three first-round picks, but it gives Miami an MVP-caliber cornerstone.

Less than two years ago, Riley was engaged in an ugly standoff with Jimmy Butler III over the All-Star forward's desire for a contract extension. Riley held firm, didn't grant the extension and eventually shipped Butler to the Warriors for an unspectacular return. While Miami took a step back without Butler and missed the playoffs last season, it's now in position to leap forward with Antetokounmpo and Adebayo. -- Golliver

The big question: Does Miami have enough surrounding its All-NBA frontcourt?

Adding Thompson, one of the best shooters in NBA history, was a huge boost, but the Heat can still use another scorer, more shooting and another playmaker to help space the floor and make things easier for Antetokounmpo and Adebayo. Also, how will the Heat offense operate with the two defensive pillars?

Coach Erik Spoelstra says adapting the offense will be made easier due to Antetokounmpo and Adebayo's competitiveness and desire to win. But it remains to be seen whether the Heat have enough shooting and scoring. If anyone can figure out the new puzzle in Miami, it will be Spoelstra. -- Youngmisuk

Post-free agency Power Rankings: Heat are 12
Summer Forecast: Projecting Miami's 2026-27
Schedule release: Biggest Heat games to watch

Basketball Power Index rank: No. 10
Here are the predicted Net Points per 100 possessions for the Heat's top seven players for the 2026-27 season.

This Heat team is an experiment in surrounding a great player (Antetokounmpo) with several mostly marginal players, an exercise Milwaukee conducted last season. The Bucks' prediction last year was for 46 wins and they actually won 32. And the Heat wins prediction for this year is ... 46. -- Dean Oliver

Read about how Net Points works here.

Biggest X factor
F Bobby Portis

Much of the focus on Miami's roster holes has centered on the team's backcourt and shooting, but an even bigger hole might exist in its frontcourt. Portis, who joined the Heat in the Antetokounmpo trade, is one of only two reserve bigs on the Heat, along with Richards, who signed as a free agent in late August.

Antetokounmpo rarely plays as a small-ball center anymore and Richards regularly posts subpar on/off numbers, so the Heat might have to rely on Portis as Adebayo's primary backup. He remains an effective offensive player, making 46% of his 3-pointers last season -- but his rim protection and overall defense might not be up to Spoelstra's standard. -- Kram

Betting insight from our expert
Bet to make ahead of the season: Antetokounmpo to win MVP (+1200)

Antetokounmpo finished in the top four in every MVP vote from 2018-19 through 2024-25, winning twice. Last season, he played a career-low 36 games as he battled injury.

If Antetokounmpo is healthy enough to play his typical minutes, he will have a massive on-court impact -- the Bucks were 14.4 points per 100 possessions better with Antetokounmpo on the court last season. And if the Heat return to top-3 contention in the East, Antetokounmpo will be among the MVP favorites. Those are a lot of ifs, but with 12-to-1 odds, Antetokounmpo is the rare MVP long shot with a tangible path to the award. -- André Snellings

Odds by DraftKings Sportsbook at time of publication.

stories.headline: What can we expect on transfer deadline day? Balogun, Enzo, Álvarez updates?
stories.summary: The summer transfer deadline closes on Sept. 1 at 6 p.m. ET for the Premier League, so here's a few things that could still happen.
stories.body:
Enzo Fernández, Julián Álvarez, Folarin Balogun and Cody Gakpo -- it sounds like a list of big performers at the 2026 Men's World Cup, but fast forward six weeks from that tournament and they are the leading names that could seal headline moves on transfer deadline day.

By the time the summer window closes at 11 p.m. BST / 6 p.m. ET on Sept 1, Premier League spending alone is likely to go past the £2.5 billion mark due to the magnitude of the deals that could still be done; a huge figure, but still short of last summer's £3.1 billion total outlay.

Manchester City's pursuit of Chelsea midfielder Fernández, who was a Premier League record transfer when he arrived at Stamford Bridge from Benfica for £106.8 million in Jan 2023, could see the Argentina international break the Premier League record again if Chelsea force City to exceed the £125 million figure that Liverpool paid to sign striker Alexander Isak from Newcastle 12 months ago.

City have already smashed their own transfer record this summer by completing a £116 million move for Nottingham Forest midfielder Elliot Anderson, but sources have said that Chelsea want a higher fee than that to land the 25-year-old Fernández, so the numbers will only go higher and higher.

If Chelsea, as expected, sanction Fernández's departure, then manager Xabi Alonso will move for Monaco's £40 million-rated Lamine Camara as his midfield replacement. But City, who signed Morocco's World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi in an £86 million deal from Lille last week, won't restrict their business just to signing Fernández.

Talks are ongoing with Liverpool over a potential £85 million deal for Netherlands forward Cody Gakpo -- a transfer unlocked by Liverpool agreeing a £123 million deal for Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola -- and Gakpo's arrival at the Etihad will enable winger Jack Grealish to take his pick of a loan move back to one of his two former teams: Everton or Aston Villa.

Everton manager David Moyes challenged his board to deliver more signings last week and the message appears to have had an effect because the Blues are closing in on a deal to re-sign Richarlison from Tottenham, will Iliman Ndiaye heading the other way to Spurs in two separate transfers rather than a swap deal.

Moyes wants to bolster his attacking options and he retains a strong interest in USMNT forward Balogun, but Everton will need to offload Beto to enable them to raise the finances to complete a €40 million move for the Monaco striker.

Forwards are often the big movers on deadline day due to clubs wanting to give themselves the insurance policy of proven goals for the season ahead. But it will take some impressive negotiations by Arsenal to convince Atlético Madrid to allow long-term target Julian Álvarez to leave the Metropolitano for the Emirates.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has been pursuing Álvarez since early last season, but Atleti have been resolute in their stance that the former Manchester City forward will not get his wish of a move to Barcelona.

Álvarez finally returned to training with Diego Simeone's squad over the weekend following a standoff with the club over his future, so the Argentina forward might now have accepted that he will not leave during this window. But sources have said that Atletico could be tempted to offload Álvarez to Arsenal if Viktor Gyökeres moves in the opposite direction, so that box-office deal could yet happen before the deadline.

If it does, Arsenal may need to balance their finances after a busy summer that has seen them sign Newcastle's Bruno Guimarães (£75 million) and Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa (£51 million), so it could raise the prospect of a surprise deadline day move for homegrown youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Arteta was adamant earlier this month that the versatile 19-year-old, who can operate at left back and in midfield, would not leave the Gunners, but Arsenal CEO Richard Garlick left the door open by admitting the club could be forced to consider offers if the "right opportunity" arose.

Chelsea and Manchester United are both interested in Lewis-Skelly and would be ready to make a late move if Arsenal suddenly displayed a readiness to do business, but right now, Lewis-Skelly looks more likely to remain at the Emirates.

United have also monitored Newcastle's Lewis Hall in their search for an upgrade on left back Luke Shaw, but the former Chelsea youngster is expected to stay at St James' Park. Having spent a relatively modest £148 million so far to land three midfielders (Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba) and a back-up goalkeeper (Karl Darlow), United are expected to be quiet on deadline day unless they can find a left back.

But United forward Joshua Zirkzee is likely to move out on loan, with Juventus and Fiorentina both interested in the former Bologna player.

Fenerbahce have a long-standing interest in Marcus Rashford, but United manager Michael Carrick has brought the England forward back into the fold following loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa and only a huge offer would now tempt United to part with the 28-year-old.

Spurs did have an interest in Rashford earlier in the window, but Roberto De Zerbi's team has completed other business and their efforts are now focused on finding clubs for Kevin Danso, Richarlison and Pape Matar Sarr.

Sunderland are in talks for Danso and Richarlison is heading back to Everton, while Juventus are negotiating for Sarr.

If Spurs can finalize all of those outgoings early enough, they may chase one more attacking signing -- they will move for Gakpo if City fail to seal a deal with Liverpool, and have also been linked with AC Milan's USMNT star Christian Pulisic -- but the likelihood is that the revolving door at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will see more exits than arrivals.

But with the clock ticking down to the deadline, the biggest focus will be on Argentina pair Fernández and Álvarez; Fernández is almost certain to happen, while Álvarez is an outside bet.

It's transfer deadline day, so don't rule anything out.

stories.headline: How to keep losing teams out of MLB playoffs
stories.summary: It's possible that we could see multiple teams with records under .500 playing this October. That's a shame.
stories.body:
On the morning of Aug. 23, if you sat down with your coffee and opened up the wild-card standings page on your ESPN app, a number of adjectives might have flooded your mind.

Strange. Weird. Wacky. Lackluster. Close. Nutty. Packed. Clustered. For me, there were two: inevitable and shameful.

On that morning, there were just four teams with winning records in the American League. Three of them were in the AL East (Tampa Bay Rays, New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox), and the other was the AL Central-leading Chicago White Sox. This wasn't an early-season fluke -- at that time there were only 35 days left in the regular season.

A quick refresher: The current MLB playoff format requires six teams per league. If the season had ended that day, we would have a sub-.500 wild-card team in the AL playoffs as the AL West winner. That's when the word "shameful" entered my mind.

But "inevitable" quickly followed, because when MLB decided to pair a 12-team playoff bracket with the expansion of interleague play, this kind of outcome became inevitable. It remains to be seen if it will happen this year, but this format means there will be losing teams in the MLB playoffs at some point.

How did we get here -- and what can we do about it?

How we got here
This all started back in 1969, when MLB first subdivided its league structure into divisions. Before that, it was literally impossible to have a playoff team without a winning record because there was no interleague play. If you have all teams in a league playing only each other, the closest you could get to this kind of scenario would be for the whole league to tie with a .500 record. But tiebreaker games would push someone into winning territory.

The possibility of a sub-.500 team getting into the playoffs during the four-division era that ran from 1969 to 1993 was likewise remote but not impossible. The 1973 Mets came the closest, winning the National League East at 82-79. The Mets grabbed sole possession of first place and reached .500 on the same day that season, Sept. 21, with only a fraction of the season remaining.

There have been two or three sub-.500 playoff teams, all coming in seasons that required an ad hoc format change because of an external intervention. The "or" in there is because of the 1981 Kansas City Royals, who went 50-53 overall during that strike-shortened season but did go 30-23 to claim the AL West's second-half crown in the one-off, split-season format.

The other two teams were products of the improvised, pandemic-shortened 2020 season, in which the playoff field was expanded to 16 teams. Both leagues fell one team short of enough .500 clubs to fill out the bracket, and so the Houston Astros and Milwaukee Brewers, both finishing 29-31, played on.

The expansion to six divisions and the introduction of wild cards into the playoff pool back in the mid-1990s increased the likelihood of a losing postseason club. Indeed, in the very first season of the six-division era, only the 1994 strike likely spared us of a sub-.500 division champion in the AL West, which featured the worst four teams, by record, in the league. When the strike hit, the Texas Rangers led the division at 52-62.

Mercifully, the subsequent years proved that kind of scenario to be a fluke, a possibility given the format but still unlikely. Both leagues have had at least six winning teams in each season of the 30-team era, a 28-year streak that is in jeopardy of being snapped this year. There have been close calls because of how the winning teams were distributed within their leagues. The 2005 San Diego Padres won the NL West at 82-80, and the 2006 champion St. Louis Cardinals won 83 games. Whew!

While the specter of a sub-.500 playoff loomed larger with the expansion to a 12-team format for the 2022 season, the odds of it happening exploded with the changes to the scheduling formula that went into effect a year later. The new docket increased the percentage of interleague games for each team from around 12.3% to 28.4 %. Now, if you had one league with a lopsided edge over the other in any given season, the end result might well be the 2026 standings.

The NL has been a much stronger circuit in 2026, for whatever reason. The senior circuit is on pace to win more than 53% of interleague matchups, and because there are so many more of those games now, that's a lot of extra wins going to the NL side. Run differentials in interleague contests underscore this year's disparity.

There are eight AL teams with at least a break-even record based on intraleague play but just five have winning marks against the NL, and no AL team is more than five games above .500 in interleague play. Meanwhile, five NL clubs are at least nine games over break-even against the AL.

Given how many teams are clustered around the .500 barrier in the AL, the daily standings will ebb and flow. Some days will reflect a losing team in playoff position, others won't. If a couple of teams get hot, we might yet be spared a losing playoff squad, but the odds that we end up on the wrong side of that are uncomfortably high.

According to my most recent run of 10,000 simulations, here is how it shook out:

Chances of ...

One sub-.500 AL playoff team: 26.1%

Two sub-.500 AL playoff teams: 1.2%

Any sub-.500 NL playoff team: 0

Sub-.500 pennant winner: 2.3%

Sub-.500 World Series champion: 0.8%

This is not good.

What we can do about it
Right now, this is not an issue at the forefront of the current dialogue between MLB owners and the MLB Players Association, but eventually it's something that could be addressed when the considerable economic disagreements between the two sides are ironed out.

There are surely some people who don't care, and that's fine. It's a matter of opinion and taste. For others, having a losing team (or teams) in the playoffs would be a further assault on the sanctity of the regular season -- the six-month marathon that is at the heart of what sets baseball apart from the other sports.

This is something that needs to be fixed, if only to amplify the incentives of teams to build a winning roster, and be willing to improve it during the season. I'd begin with an overriding, ironclad rule:

A .500 record is the minimum winning percentage a team must achieve to qualify for the postseason.

When the current format can't be filled out because of that rule, we have to figure something else out.

Here are six suggestions. I'd guess the odds against any of these being implemented are long. Still, let's plant some hypothetical seeds.

Option 1: Drop playoff slots that would be filled by a losing team

You have just five teams reach the .500 mark in a league? Fine. You get five playoff spots. The team that otherwise would have played a seed held by a losing team advances to the next round.

In a vacuum, this is my favorite option. It's simple and clean. It also adds a measure of drama as teams jostling for playoff spots are battling not just each other but also that qualifying standard of .500. It preserves the lines between the leagues, such as they are. It gives a bye to the team playing the 6-seed, assuming they are only short one team. That team would be the No. 3 seed, the third division champion that in the current format doesn't get enough of a reward.

The problem with this idea is pretty obvious: MLB has broadcast contracts to carry a certain stock of playoff games, and not playing those games would be something of an issue.

Option 2: Draft from another division or league

If you win a division with a losing record, congratulations. That division title flag is your only reward -- because your division doesn't get a playoff slot.

Most seasons, you would be able to simply take a winning team from another division to fill the spot, one that otherwise would be on the outside.

But what if there weren't enough winning teams to do that? What if we didn't have enough winning teams to give us a full set of non-losing wild-card teams? Then we have to look at the other league, which presumably would have demonstrated a clear-enough edge in interleague play to create this problem in the first place.

During the 30-team era so far, there has been just one instance in which a league did not have at least six winning teams. That was the AL in 2017, when leagues still only needed five teams to fill out a bracket. If we had needed a sixth team that year, we would have had one of three teams finishing 80-82 -- the Royals, Rays and Los Angeles Angels. That doesn't help.

Over in the NL that season, seven clubs won at least 83 games, the worst of which was St. Louis at 83-79. So we simply slide St. Louis over to the AL for that season's playoff.

This season, that would mean the playoff chances of the Padres and Arizona Diamondbacks, currently battling for the NL's 6-seed, would go up dramatically. Meanwhile, new life would be breathed into the chances of the Cardinals, Miami Marlins and Pittsburgh Pirates.

The more teams from which you have to choose, the lesser the chance you have to choose one with a losing record, mitigating the unintended consequences of the interleague-heavy schedule. During the 30-team era, there have been at least 12 non-losing teams every season, and the average has been 15.5.

Is this perfect? It would mean, for example, that the Cardinals and Chicago Cubs could meet in the World Series. As a baseball history nut and something of a traditionalist, I wouldn't love that. But I would hate it less than having a 79-83 team in the World Series.

Besides, we've had to get used to a persistent blurring of the lines between the leagues over the past three decades. This would just be another step along those lines. We've seen the 1982 AL champion Brewers become a fixture in the NL playoffs and a division rival of the Cardinals, the team they played in that long-ago Fall Classic. We've seen the Astros win pennants in both leagues.

The league distinctions are going to continue to erode. For me, that's what underscores the change in scheduling formula. It's a frog-boiling situation. When baseball expands, it's likely that the leagues as we've known them are only going to be further scrambled. Allowing a team to switch leagues to fill out an otherwise lackluster playoff bracket is just another step in that direction.

Option 3: Vastly increase the difficulty of the road for sub-.500 teams

This wouldn't ban losing teams per se, but it would greatly add to their incentive for getting to .500 before their playoff journey begins.

Use ghost wins -- i.e., the losing team has to spot its opponent a win at the start of the series. Don't give losing teams any home playoff games, even if they survive the wild-card round. The ghost win follows them through each round of the postseason they reach.

While this wouldn't erase enough of the chances for a losing team to make the playoffs for my taste, it would at least minimize the chances of it getting to the World Series. Better than nothing.

Option 4: Use only intraleague records to determine playoff slots

This is a thing that exists in American sports, so I'll throw it out there even though I don't like it. Just as the SEC, for example, crowns its football champion based on conference games only, so would the AL and NL decide their playoff brackets only on intraleague games.

This would be reflected in the standings, so maybe you could overlook an overall losing record because it's the league record that matters.

Option 5: Kill the leagues and divisions

You have a 30-team scrum and a schedule that is all about jostling for postseason seeding. This isn't what baseball has ever been, and I'm personally not a fan, but it is simple and clears up any hand-wringing about superior teams ending up in a subservient playoff position because of the format.

Option 6: Fix the schedule

You could use any of the first four options above in conjunction with this. Put the interleague schedule back the way it was or even reduce it from that. Increase the number of games between teams battling for the same playoff spots. Increase the number of games between league and division foes down the stretch. No more last-week interleague games. I am very much in favor of doing this.

Ideas to avoid a season like this, and its possible consequences, can get pretty weird pretty fast. But you don't have to get wacky, weird or even nutty to get there. You just have to avoid being shameful.

stories.headline: Concussion saga not a distraction for finals-bound Cats
stories.summary: Geelong players are adamant the AFL club's concussion saga hasn't been a distraction as the Cats gear up for finals while relishing Jake Kolodjashnij's return to the fold.
stories.body:
Geelong players are adamant the AFL club's concussion saga hasn't been a distraction as the Cats gear up for finals while relishing Jake Kolodjashnij's return to the fold.

The Cats were last week fined $140,000 for failing to officially let the AFL know about the concussion waiver in Kolodjashnij's contract.

The penalty is $100,000 plus a suspended sanction of $40,000, which stems from the league fining Geelong last October after an investigation into the club's third-party agreements.

Kolodjashnij, who came forward as the player involved shortly after the story broke and has not played at any level since, returned to the club last week ahead of the finals.

When asked about Kolodjashnij's return, midfielder Tom Atkins, the defender's 2022 premiership teammate, said: "Awesome. Kola's one of my favourite teammates, so yeah, to see him back, feeling a bit better.

"Obviously we'd love him to be back playing and back in training, but hopefully that can get itself sorted soon.

"But just having him in the rooms and seeing him smiling again is good."

Asked on Monday whether he or another player had a discussion around a similar concussion agreement, Atkins said: "No".

The experienced midfielder indicated the concussion saga, and last week's handing down of a fine, hadn't been discussed with the players.

"No, it's very much been, our focus has been performing on the weekends, and yeah, we just wanted to make sure Kola was alright as teammates and as friends," Atkins said.

"That's probably the extent of the detail that we looked into it as players. So yeah, just care for Kola, that's pretty much it."

Geelong start their September campaign in Friday night's blockbuster elimination final against Carlton at the MCG.

Asked whether the concussion saga had been a distraction, Atkins said: "not at all.

"Each individual's different, but I think Jake himself - that's the last thing he'd want - to distract from our performance.

"And I think it's a good quality of our playing group is we're mature and we're able to compartmentalise a bit.

"So we can show care for Jake during the week, but we can also put that to the side and perform on the weekend. I think we've done that."

stories.headline: Lando Norris signs new contract to stay at McLaren until at least 2030
stories.summary: Reigning world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a new contract to remain at the team until at least 2030.
stories.body:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a new contract to remain at the team until at least 2030.

The deal, which includes one of his title-winning Formula 1 cars as a gift from the team, also has the option of a "multiyear" extension beyond 2030.

Norris, 26, who made his F1 debut with McLaren in 2019, last signed a multiyear contract extension in 2024 that was believed to run until 2027.

Norris' future at McLaren had not looked in doubt and was only cemented by his championship-winning season in 2025, which made him the first driver since Lewis Hamilton in 2008 to win F1's top prize with the team.

The new contract represents a trend in long-term commitments between star drivers and teams in this year's driver market after Max Verstappen committed to Red Bull until 2030 last week and Charles Leclerc signed a new multiyear deal with Ferrari earlier this season.

"McLaren is my home, and I'm very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030," Norris said. "When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win Championships.

"We've achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we're capable of achieving it. I can't wait to get back in the car in Monza and I'm very excited about what the future holds for us, both over the rest of this season, and in the coming years."

- Max vs 100: Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

- Despite back-to-back wins, Norris says his F1 title form is a mirage

- F1 2027 driver lineups: Who has a seat - and who's out of contract?

Norris' teammate Oscar Piastri extended his contact at the start of the 2025 season and is believed to be committed to the team until at least 2028.

Despite conversations between McLaren's senior management and Verstappen earlier this season, the team has always publicly stated its commitment to Norris and Piastri.

Team principal Andrea Stella used the contract announcement to reiterate his belief that McLaren has one of the strongest driver pairings in F1.

"Lando has been an integral part of McLaren's journey and success over the last nine years, and we are delighted to continue our partnership with him through to at least 2030," Stella said. "He is an exceptional driver, someone who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren, but above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team.

"Since joining McLaren as part of our junior programme, he has grown with us and played a central role in bringing the team back to the front of Formula 1. This extension gives us important continuity and reinforces our confidence in the direction we are taking together. With him and Oscar, we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1."

As part of his new deal, Norris will receive one of the MCL39 cars that he used to secure his first F1 title in 2025.

"This gift serves a lasting reminder of his contribution to the team, in particular his part in securing the team's second consecutive Constructors' title in 2025, while also becoming the team's first Formula 1 Drivers' World Champion since 2008," a team statement said.

stories.headline: Every time Messi scored 4 goals for Barcelona, Inter Miami, Argentina
stories.summary: Lionel Messi grabbed the headlines on Saturday by scoring four goals in Inter Miami's 7-1 win over Montréal. But the feat is nothing new for the GOAT.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi grabbed the headlines on Saturday by scoring four goals for reigning MLS champions Inter Miami CF in their 7-1 win over CF Montréal.

But, for a player who has scored more than 900 goals in a trophy-laden career for Argentina, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami, the feat is nothing new.

In fact, the eight-time winner of the Ballon d'Or has scored a "poker" no fewer than nine times to date. And, on a couple of those occasions, he netted even more than four.

- Messi tracker: Goals, assists, moments for Miami, Argentina

Here are highlights of every single time that the GOAT has done the GOATiest of GOAT things.

1. Barcelona 4-1 Arsenal, Champions League (April 6, 2010)

On a big night for Messi (and a bad one for Arsenal goalkeeper Wojciech Szczesny), Messi hit the first four-goal haul of his career in a UEFA Champions League quarterfinal second leg to move into the ranks of Barcelona's top 10 goal scorers of all-time.

2. Barcelona 5-1 Valencia, LaLiga (Feb. 19, 2012)

Messi had to wait almost two full years for his next "poker," but when it came it was a fine way to mark his 200th appearance in LaLiga for Barça.

3. Barcelona 7-1 Bayer Leverkusen, Champions League (March 7, 2012)

In 2012, Messi was in the best form of his career, and it only took him a couple more weeks to score four goals again. In fact, he was so hot, that he scored five in one match against poor old Leverkusen.

4. Barcelona 4-0 Espanyol, LaLiga (May 5, 2012) (Pep's final game)

Messi capped off an incredible 2011-12 season in the final game by netting his 50th league goal of the campaign. That landmark came as part of his latest four-goal haul, on Pep Guardiola's last match as Barcelona coach.

5. Barcelona 5-1 Osasuna, LaLiga (Jan. 27, 2013)

The following year, Messi scored his 200th LaLiga strike as part of a four-goal salvo. This match was the 11th game of a scoring streak that would eventually extend to 19 matches.

6. Barcelona 6-1 Eibar, LaLiga (Sept. 19, 2017)

Messi knows how to time the delivery of his "poker" performances to hit personal milestones. His next one included his 300th goal scored at Camp Nou.

7. Barcelona 5-0 Eibar, LaLiga (Feb. 22, 2020)

Eibar were again the victims of a Messi scoring blitz in 2020, and this time they could only praise their tormentor. After the match, the club posted on social media: "We suffer you, we put up with you, we endure you. And we have no choice but to stand up and applaud you."

8. Argentina vs. Estonia, international friendly (June 5, 2022)

Why Argentina were playing Estonia in Spanish city of Pamplona, we can't really say. But we do know that he became the first male player to score four goals in a single Champions League game and a senior international match that night. Six months later, he led them to FIFA World Cup glory.

9. Inter Miami CF 7-1 CF Montréal, MLS (Aug. 29, 2026)

It took another four years but, at the age of 39, Messi is still capable of posting those big numbers.

"I'll say it again: I don't have any qualifiers for such soccer beauty," Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos said postmatch. "There are so many things combined that leave you at a loss for words, no?

"I don't think he's a normal soccer player."

We couldn't agree more.

stories.headline: Cris Cyborg is still going strong as a force in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: At age 41, PFL women's featherweight champion continues win streak to secure spot in ESPN P4P top 10.
stories.body:
Cris Cyborg is an MMA legend. Period. End of story.

Actually, the Cyborg story continues, even with her being 41 years old and having spent 21 years in the sport. A champion in an unprecedented five fight promotions, she has long been a fixture in the ESPN pound-for-pound women's rankings. And by posting her 30th career victory -- the most ever by a woman in MMA -- at PFL Tampa on Saturday to retain the women's featherweight championship, Cyborg solidified her hold on the No. 3 spot.

It wasn't easy, not like so many past Cyborg fights in which she aggressively bowled over opponents to score quick knockouts. Ketlen Vieira put up a fight, bloodying Cyborg's face and achieving controlling positions on the canvas several times. But Cyborg persevered, nearly doubling Vieira's strike output and earning a unanimous decision win. As a result, the ESPN voting panel kept her right where she was in the top three.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Aug. 26. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko has more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and now she's established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira on Saturday as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 4

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: TBA

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

6. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-2

Last: W (TKO1) vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius, Oct. 18, 2025

Next: Sept. 12 vs. Alexa Grasso

Fiorot has handled everyone the UFC has put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But Fiorot could earn another shot at the belt if she can get past Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

9. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

10. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 17-5-1

Last: W (KO) vs. Maycee Barber, March 28

Next: Sept. 12 vs. Manon Fiorot

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. That made the fight with Barber a must-win, and Grasso came through explosively. Next up is Fiorot, a fellow title contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Manon Fiorot; 6. Dakota Ditcheva; 7. Natalia Silva; 8. Erin Blanchfield; 9. Tatiana Suarez; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Ditcheva; 5. Dern; 6. Silva; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.
